hook: Three messages I never type anymore
caption:
Three messages I used to type every week. I haven't typed any of them in months.

1. Pricing. Someone asks what I charge, and the answer goes out in seconds — same wording I'd use, sent without me opening anything.

2. The follow-up. A deal goes quiet, and the check-in fires on schedule instead of sitting on my mental to-do list until I feel guilty enough to send it.

3. The invoice. Work gets marked done, the invoice goes out. No end-of-week ritual, no forgotten payment.

None of this is clever. It's the same words I was already writing — just written once instead of forty times.

That's the part people miss about automating a solo business. You're not replacing your judgment. You're removing the typing that sits between a decision and the thing actually happening.

Which message do you retype the most? Tell me in the comments — I'll show you how I'd automate that one.
